# GCIP Cloud Function Sample

Sample apps are provided in the `sample/http` directory to
demonstrate various
[blocking functions](http://cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/blocking-functions)
functionalities:

**Before Create Event**
- Block sign up of users with no email.
- Block sign up of users with a specific disallowed domain.
- Set claims from IdP (eg. employee ID) as a custom claim on the user.
- Treat certain IdPs as verified (eg. GitHub.com).

**Before Sign In Event**
- Set placeholder image and display name during sign in when none are
  available.
- Update session claims with the user role and session IP address.

To deploy a test sample for `beforeCreate` and `beforeSignIn`,
run from the root directory:

```bash
cd sample/http/cjs
```

Enable Cloud Functions for your project following Google Cloud Functions
[instructions](https://cloud.google.com/functions/docs/tutorials/http).

Install `gcloud` SDK. Follow the instructions:
- [For MacOS](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/quickstart-macos)
- [For Linux](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/quickstart-linux)

You will need to initialize `gcloud` via command line:

```bash
gcloud init
# Update components to latest.
gcloud components update
```

Modify the functions in `index.js` as needed.

Deploy the functions:

```bash
gcloud functions deploy beforeCreate --runtime nodejs14 --trigger-http \
--allow-unauthenticated
gcloud functions deploy beforeSignIn --runtime nodejs14 --trigger-http \
--allow-unauthenticated
```

Register the functions with your
[GCIP](https://cloud.google.com/identity-platform/) project.

- In the Identity Platform Cloud Console section
- Go to the **Settings** menu
- In the **Triggers** tab, click the drop down menu for the relevant event
  (`beforeCreate`, `beforeSignin` or both) for which you want to trigger your
  cloud function.
- Select the deployed HTTP triggers (`beforeCreate`, `beforeSignin`) from the
  event drop down menu.
- Click **Save** to complete.

An ES6 version with modules is also available in the `sample/http/esm`
directory.
